# Caddy (HTTPS) — root-context-sse

App at /, Caddy terminates TLS on https://localhost:9443/ and forwards over plain HTTP, PUSH over Server-Sent Events. SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY=NATIVE so the push URL is built with the https scheme and the browser does not block the event stream as mixed content.

Proxy URL on `https://localhost:9443`: `/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

Caddy site block (`caddy/https/root-context-sse/vaadin.caddyfile`), mounted as
`/etc/caddy/vaadin.caddyfile`:

```caddyfile
# App at /, Caddy terminates TLS on https://localhost:9443/ and forwards over
# plain HTTP, PUSH over Server-Sent Events.
#
# https/root-context plus the refusal from templates/passthrough-sse.caddyfile.
# Over HTTP/2 the event stream is one stream on a shared connection rather than
# a connection of its own, and the refusal is moot there anyway — h2 has no
# Upgrade header to carry — but a browser that falls back to HTTP/1.1 is still
# answered 501.
:443 {
	tls /etc/caddy/tls/localhost.crt /etc/caddy/tls/localhost.key
	import common

	@upgrade header Upgrade *
	respond @upgrade 501

	reverse_proxy vaadin:8080
}
```

The global options and the `common` snippet this file imports (the
access log and the compression allowlist) come from the shared
[Caddyfile](../../Caddyfile), mounted read-only over the image's own
`/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`. It imports this file, so the two only load as a pair.
